thread:
morgan: heads up - we're seeing a spike of SAML signature validation failures in prod auth-audit. started ~10:12 UTC. multiple customers affected. error = \"Invalid signature\". possible tamper or idp key mismatch.
ellie: copying logs? any recent idp cert/key rotations? :eyes:
morgan: paste — auth-audit shows repeated entries like:\n```\n2026-03-21T10:12:05Z ERROR saml: assertion validation failed user=alice@example.com err=InvalidSignature key_kid=Yk7f... request_id=abc123
2026-03-21T10:12:06Z ERROR saml: assertion validation failed user=bob@example.com err=InvalidSignature key_kid=Yk7f... request_id=abc124
``` 
satya: @morgan quick check — did we push any change to saml verifier or KMS? deploy-bot shows a config push at 09:58 by riley but no runtime deploys.
riley: i pushed a metadata fetch backfill script at 09:55 to run hourly, it only reads idp metadata and caches jwk sets. not supposed to touch keys. i can revert if needed.
ellie: kms-bot, any recent rekeys or alias rotations for idp-signing-key? kms-bot: automated message — no customer KMS rekey events in last 24h; last rotate 2026-02-10.
sec-oncall-bot: incident created #INC-2026-187; paging sec-oncall.
satya: ok, let's triage: 1) confirm if failing kid matches any JWK in our cached set; 2) compare idp metadata on origin (okta/azure) vs our cache; 3) check clock skew and replay.
morgan: i already checked — key_kid Yk7f is NOT in our cached JWKs. but the raw SAML assertion includes KeyInfo with that kid.
riley: running a live metadata fetch now against idp metadata URL.
riley: fetched metadata shows two signing keys: Yk7f (new) and Rv3a (old). our cache only has Rv3a. backfill script must have failed on the last run and left stale cache.
ellie: that explains InvalidSignature. is it because the metadata fetch timed out earlier and we didn't reload? which last-success timestamp on cache?
morgan: cache metadata_last_fetch=2026-03-21T02:14:03Z — oh yikes, it's stale. script log shows 504 from idp at ~02:10 and we didn't retry.
satya: impact: assertions signed with new key Yk7f fail until we trust it. mitigation: 1) add Yk7f to cache immediately, 2) fail-open? no, can't. safer to accept both keys.
riley: pushing one-off job to reload JWK set now. will post results.
riley: done — cache updated with Yk7f. monitoring.
morgan: auth-audit errors dropping back to baseline. confirmed end-to-end for affected users.
ellie: root cause: one-off metadata fetch transient failure + backfill script didn't retry and left stale cache while IdP rotated keys earlier today. follow-ups: - make metadata fetch resilient with exponential backoff and immediate retry on 5xx - add alert if >5 saml invalid signatures/min for 5 min - instrument cache freshness and surface in console - update runbook for idp rekey handling.
satya: also check SCIM provisioning paths — if idp rotates keys frequently it may affect any signed SCIM callbacks (we don't use signed SCIM currently). add note for customers using signed assertions.
sec-oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-187 severity set to P2. incident owner assigned: ellie.
morgan: quick security note for vuln triage: no evidence of tampering or MITM; all traces point to legitimate Okta rekey. we still need to confirm audit export lines to show which customers saw failed auth attempts for postmortem.iley: i'll open a follow-up ticket with affected org IDs and TTL for recovery window. tagging infra to add cache eviction metric.
ellie: postmortem steps and timeline will be created; propose SLA change to auto-retry metadata fetch 3x and fallback to live fetch on validation failure.
morgan: closing thread when postmortem doc is in. thanks all :thumbsup:
